sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (bijural): Common Law for federal public law and criminal law; Civil Law for private law matters in Quebec, including partnership and corporate governance
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 29; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, C.Q.L.R. c. P-45; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; and applicable FINTRAC Compliance Policies and Interpretations, together with the Quebec Civil Code articles on the société en commandite (limited partnership).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent corporate status certificate for each non-resident general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent authority in the general partner's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each individual by beneficial ownership determination
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent licensing authority in the individual's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, register of directors, and register of officers of the general partner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the general partner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the local Quebec-based representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the grantor is located

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the source of funds and business relationship for each initial capital contributor
Professional qualification certificate and curriculum vitae of the proposed general partner or fund manager, evidencing competence in revenue-based financing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: University, professional association, or certifying body

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against (i) Canada's Consolidated Sanctions List published under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; and (iv) FINTRAC-relevant domestic and international PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for all beneficial owners holding 25% or more, including source-of-funds verification, adverse media review, and annual re-screening. All screening must be documented and retained per FINTRAC record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) – Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (C.Q.L.R. c. C-11), every enterprise name used in Quebec must be expressed in French. A Latin-alphabet transliteration without accents is accepted, but any non-French component must be accompanied by a French version that is given precedence. Names shall not be misleading, contrary to public order, or substantially identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated according to an officially recognized romanization standard and certified by a sworn translator.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may, within 30 days of the refusal notice, file an administrative review request with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, attaching a revised proposed name, a French-language compliance certificate, and evidence of prior user authorization. If the administrative review fails, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days of the reconsideration decision. A successful appeal results in a fresh 90-day reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are not permissible as the sole registered office for a Quebec limited partnership engaged in revenue-based financing. A physical establishment in Quebec is required under the Civil Code of Quebec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. The physical office must be staffed and accessible during ordinary business hours, and may serve as the place where corporate records, UBO registers, and AML/CFT files are held.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months following registration, and an annual probability of not less than 35% thereafter, given the medium-risk enhanced AML classification applied to non-dilutive revenue-based financing entities under FINTRAC risk assessment guidance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (C.Q.L.R. c. P-45)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) initial registration declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff for declaration of registration of a limited partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents (per bundle of 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority for authentication in the country of origin (e.g., Global Affairs Canada or provincial authentication service for Canadian-origin documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing government schedule of fees per apostille certificate and agency service charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French-language translation of incorporation documents, UBO declarations, and AML platform documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for certified legal translation, quoted per page and per language pair

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered physical office in Quebec — first year arrangement fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local office leasing provider or registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial lease and service benchmark for financial-sector registered offices in Quebec

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT and UBO compliance framework drafting, including partnership agreement alignment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for specialized AML and partnership law compliance drafting in Montreal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, sanctions, and adverse media screening software subscription and initial batch screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual subscription fee and per-screening data fee under FINTRAC-approved screening services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Administrative appeal and name clearance contingency reserve
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and external counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Estimated hourly legal rate plus statutory reconsideration application fee, if required

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2186 et seq. (contract of partnership) and arts. 2236 et seq. (limited partnership); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 21 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Enterprises of Quebec)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account or compulsory capital deposit is required. The partnership agreement must specify each partner's capital contribution in money, property or services; limited partners lose limited liability if they take part in the management of the partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED by the general partner of [LP Name] (the 'Partnership') that: 1. The general partner hereby subscribes to its limited partnership interest for CAD [amount], such subscription being accepted, acknowledged in the Partnership capital and reflected in the declaration required by the Civil Code of Québec. 2. The registered office of the Partnership in Québec is fixed at [address], and the Registrar of Enterprises of Québec will be notified as required. 3. [Name] is appointed authorised manager and representative, with authority to open bank accounts, execute financing documents and file declarations. 4. No directors are appointed because the Partnership is a limited partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification and drafting of partnership documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name-search and drafting support
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed enterprise name for distinctiveness and compliance with Quebec's legal publicity rules. Prepare the French-language declaration and the partnership agreement; if the partners are unable to obtain an acceptable name, modify the distinctive element and resubmit in the same session.
required_dossiers: Proposed enterprise name
Name-search verification report
Draft partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Identification and capital contribution summary for all general and limited partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or refused, immediately revise the name with a new distinctive or geographic element and resubmit; no governmental fee is forfeited on a pre-filing name search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of partnership agreement and notarization if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary or external legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the partnership agreement in writing and have all general and limited partners sign. Notarization is mandatory only if a contribution consists of an immovable; for cash or service contributions, a signed private writing suffices. Keep the original and a copy in the Partnership's records.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Contributions in money, property or services
Power of attorney if signing by an authorised representative
Notarial deed for immovable contribution, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or legal counsel identifies a defective signature or incomplete schedules, execute corrected signature pages and re-sign the agreement; no registry objection is triggered at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and transmit the Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership, pay the prescribed filing fee, and disclose the registered office, general partner identification, limited partners' contributions, and the authorized representative for service of notices. Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and attestation of registration.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership
Identification and residential/business addresses of general partners
List or schedule of limited partners' contributions
Proof of signing authority for the filing representative
Payment of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries or rejects the declaration, download the notice of discrepancy from the online account, correct the stated fields, and resubmit within the prescribed delay; if needed, request a formal review of the Registrar's decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for GST/HST and QST where the CAD 30,000 annual threshold applies, or voluntarily where invoicing requires it. If the Partnership will employ staff, open a CRA payroll account and a Revenu Québec individual source deduction account. The general partner acts as the agent for tax registration purposes.
required_dossiers: Attestation of registration and NEQ
Executed partnership agreement
CRA GST/HST and business-number registration form
Revenu Québec QST registration form
Payroll account opening information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec rejects an account application because of inconsistent business data, verify the data at the Registraire des entreprises, correct any mismatch, and resubmit; call the taxpayer service window for expedited resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation governance and AML/KYC record keeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and internal governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first resolution of the general partner, appoint the authorized manager, open bank accounts, and establish the registered office records. Because the fund operates in non-dilutive revenue-based financing, it is not a deposit-taking institution and does not require a financial services operating licence; nevertheless, implement enhanced AML/KYC policies consistent with the Medium-Risk_Enhanced classification and maintain a partner register.
required_dossiers: First resolution of the general partner
Bank account opening documentation
AML/KYC internal policy
Register of partners and limited partnership interests
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or counterparty asks for further KYC evidence, execute additional confirmation certificates signed by the general partner and supplement the partner register; if an AML regulator issue arises, engage counsel to update the compliance program.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal permits and inspections department of the Quebec municipality where the registered office is located; no provincial industrial licensing board applies because the fund is an administrative, non-manufacturing business.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal occupancy certificate (certificat d'occupation) issued by the local municipality; no provincial operating or manufacturing permit is applicable to a revenue-based financing fund.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category D – administrative office use only; no Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC emissions or regulated air pollutants are generated by the financing fund's administrative operations. Sanitary sewage discharge must meet the applicable municipal sewer by-law; residual waste management must comply with the Quebec Residual Materials Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 35).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Quebec Fire Safety Code, structural load verification through the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) when applicable, municipal occupancy inspection, and registration with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for any employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - My Business Account portal at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html; Revenu Québec - Espace Entreprises portal at revenuquebec.ca (for QST and provincial income tax)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the limited partnership as a société en commandite with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Complete CRA Form RC1 to acquire the partnership Business Number (BN) and open the federal RT account (income tax), GST/HST account, and payroll accounts as needed. Using the BN, register the partnership with Revenu Québec for QST through the Espace Entreprises portal. Non-resident partners must appoint a service address in Quebec and comply with section 129 of the Quebec Taxation Act; the LP must also obtain a T5013 partnership information return filing number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime; the LP is mandatorily fiscally transparent for federal and Quebec income tax under Income Tax Act s.96 and the Quebec Taxation Act. Available elections include a partnership fiscal period election under ITA s.249.1 and a partner-level phased income election. The LP may also elect GST/HST group treatment under ETA s.156 and the QST equivalent, and may consider the hybrid-mismatch election rules in ITA ss.18.4-18.6 and related Quebec provisions to prevent double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and QST (dual value-added tax systems)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable worldwide supplies for GST/HST, and CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies in Quebec for QST. Financial services supplied by the fund are exempt supplies, so a partnership whose only taxable turnover is exempt financial services may remain unregistered despite exceeding the threshold; voluntary registration may still be sought to claim input tax refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government API approval or digital stamping exists in Canada at the federal or Quebec level. Electronic invoices are permitted if accessible in a legible, readable format and contain the mandatory prescribed particulars (seller identity, BN, date, description, tax amounts). The federal and Quebec e-invoicing framework is voluntary and follows PEPPOL-BIS 3.0 interoperability without mandatory pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated when exported from Canada under a customs export declaration. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident recipient and not supplied to, or consumed by, any person in Canada. For a royalty-financing fund, revenue-based financing or royalty transactions with non-resident digital brands will generally constitute exempt financial supplies unless structured as exported services under Schedule VI Part V s.7 of the Excise Tax Act and the corresponding QST regulation; the taxpayer must substantiate the non-resident status, foreign use, and place of supply, including a written contract identifying the recipient and the service description.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canadian Export Report / Form B13A) for physical goods; for pure services, an export declaration is not applicable
Bill of Lading or other contract of carriage evidencing physical removal from Canada; for services, the signed financing royalty agreement and evidence of delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/FX wire confirmation documenting the non-resident's payment
Recipient non-resident status certificate or equivalent tax residence evidence if relied upon for zero-rating
Detailed GST/HST/QST-compliant invoice showing the supply description, rate basis and zero-rated nature
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rated supply at the combined 14.975% rate where contemporaneous documentary proof is deficient, adding statutory interest and penalties for late reporting. Gross negligence carries a civil penalty of up to 50% of the tax evaded under the Income Tax Act and parallel Quebec rules; fraudulent zero-rating or refund schemes are indictable offenses with fines up to 200% of the tax attempted to be avoided and imprisonment. Refunds may be clawed back plus interest if documentation is manufactured or the underlying export never occurred.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); the Department of Finance (Canada/FINTRAC) administers no separate foreign exchange control agency, and OSFI supervises federally regulated banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction with fully free convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. There are no foreign exchange controls or mandatory approvals for inward capital contributions, profit remittances, royalty payments, or financing-fund distributions by a non-resident LP. Profit remittance is governed principally by tax compliance: Part XIII withholding at source (e.g. 25% Canadian statutory withholding on dividends, interest, rents, or royalties to non-residents, subject to treaty reduction under the Canada-US Tax Treaty where applicable), rather than exchange-control restrictions. Québec also applies its own provincial withholding and reporting obligations under the Taxation Act (Quebec).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no surrender rule, statutory timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Canada. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency indefinitely. Reporting obligations are limited to general AML/CFT rules: financial institutions must report electronic transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and the Canada Border Services Agency collects trade data with underlying paperwork preserved. No central bank approval is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability for cross-border use in Canada. Canada does not recognize the European 'EMI' or electronic-money-institution vertical as a bank-regulated category. A foreign EMI cannot take deposits in Canada without becoming a bank; it may operate only as a registered money-services business (MSB) with FINTRAC if it carries on remittance or foreign-exchange dealing in Canada. Digital EMIs can be practical only as an ancillary payment-rail provider behind a tier-1 Canadian bank account, not as the primary clearing or custody bank for an LP royalty-financing fund. Québec's financial-licensing regime under the AMF may further constrain unlicensed fintech inbound activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banking policy generally requires a face-to-face identity verification interview for non-resident entities, particularly for a limited partnership with non-resident or corporate general partners. Physical attendance at a bank branch is the default mandate, but many tier-1 banks permit remote online onboarding if executed through a notarized corporate resolution, apostilled documents, Canadian legal counsel certification, and an enhanced due-diligence video interview. Québec branch requirements are more exacting with civil-law notarization. For a medium-risk royalty-financing fund, an in-person or notarized remote KYC interview conducted by a licensed Canadian lawyer or notary is strongly recommended to avoid rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partnership with no physical substance in Canada or Québec
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete LP agreement and registration certificate; certificate of existence from home jurisdiction; beneficial-ownership schedule with all partners and 25%-or-more ultimate owners; Canadian tax-filings confirmation; proof of legitimate commercial purpose; corporate registry abstracts; notarized board/general-partner resolution authorizing account openers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-based financing receivables from digital brands with high cross-border e-commerce flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed royalty-financing contracts, invoice schedules, sales-royalty calculations, audited payment statements, bank statements of in-flowing royalties, source-of-wealth declarations for investors, and a clear statistical description of expected transaction velocity and counterparty geography.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth opacity on capital injection from foreign investors or a parent fund
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fund-side audited financial statements; investor AML/KYC files; bank references; proof of transfer chain; legal-entity ownership breakdown; sworn declarations for each material contributor; public registries or SEC/regulatory excerpts for regulated overseas fund vehicles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (payments from sanctioned or monitored territory, or high-risk e-commerce merchants)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country- and merchant-level sanctions screening reports; adverse-media mitigation memo; export-control and sanctions compliance policy; FINTRAC and OSFI-aligned AML/ATF policy; transaction-monitoring agreement; risk-based action under Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of statutory license for 'royalty financing fund' (ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525990)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming that royalty/revenue-based financing does not constitute deposit-taking, lending in the regulated credit context, or securities dealing in Canada when executed on a private-fund basis; securities-law advice regarding prospectus exemptions in Québec; confirmation of no requirement for a statutory financial-services license; jurisdiction-specific fund/private-fund memorandum.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound equity/capital contributions into the Québec LP, use a SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) from the sending bank to the Canadian beneficiary bank, with Field 50K remitter, Field 59 beneficiary account, and Field 70 remittance information. Canada does not use numeric central-bank purpose codes for FX-control purposes, but the bank will demand a clear economic-purpose string such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / ROYALTY FINANCING FUND / LP INVESTMENT' and may file a FINTRAC EFT report for any amount equal to or above CAD 10,000. To satisfy bank verification, include the signed LP certificate, source-of-funds evidence, capital account statement, and confirmation that the inbound transfer is a contribution to partnership equity and not a loan requiring Part XIII withholding. No exchange-control permission is needed, but non-resident limited partners must file Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) information returns where required and any Québec registration returns.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements and royalty payments should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct beneficiary payments, with MT202 COVER for correspondent-bank routing if requested. For documentary trade, commercial letters of credit (LCs) issued by a Canadian tier-1 bank under UCP600 are appropriate for physical-goods or digital-brand supply-chain settlements. For recurring royalty streams, ACH or wire payment rails through the primary corporate operating account are permissible but require standard FINTRAC threshold reporting and robust invoice-level back-up. Where the LP sponsors merchant cash-advance-style disbursements to brands, use the same wire rails with escrowed-collection arrangements; direct-debit (ACH pre-authorized debits) can be implemented for Canadian-domiciled merchants only after PCMLTFA-compliant payment-credential verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (deliverable CAD vs USD/EUR/GBP) with a Canadian Schedule I bank or registered dealer
Vanilla FX options (European-style call/put) for downside protection on royalty streams
FX swaps (swap of principal and interest flows in two currencies) for short-term liquidity conversion
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) permitted for long-term revenue-based financing liabilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or non-convertible currencies, permissible for hedging emerging-market royalty receivables
Plain-vanilla cross-currency swap arrangements executed under ISDA documentation with a Qualified Counterparty in Canada

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual, within 60 days of the anniversary of the initial registration date of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may cause the registrar to issue a notice and strike the enterprise from the register; penalties for late or false annual declarations range from CAD 200 to CAD 2,000 for individuals and CAD 500 to CAD 5,000 for legal persons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar year-end partnerships with only Canadian-resident partners: March 31; partnerships with any non-resident partner: 5 months after the partnership fiscal period-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is CAD 25 per partner per day up to a maximum of CAD 100 days, subject to a minimum of CAD 100 and a maximum of CAD 2,100 per partner; continued non-compliance may trigger fines or prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit is imposed by the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises for a private limited partnership; a statutory audit is required only if the partnership agreement mandates it, if the entity becomes a reporting issuer, or if securities or financial-services regulations impose audited financial statements. This revenue-based financing fund does not require a statutory licence and therefore has no regulator-imposed audit threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) applies to a private limited partnership; IFRS is permitted and generally required if the partnership is publicly accountable or if an investment-fund style financial statement is prepared using IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law does not require a separate annual UBO filing for a limited partnership; the REQ annual declaration must be updated and confirmed annually and must reflect any change in the general partner or, where relevant, the limited partners. Any change in partners, including a transfer of units, must be reported to the Registraire within 60 days of the change. The internal register of limited partners must be maintained continuously and updated upon each transfer of an interest. The general partner corporation, if incorporated under the CBCA or the QBCA, must separately maintain an individuals-with-significant-control register and comply with any applicable annual confirmation obligations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners and Contributions
Minute Book or Resolution Register of the General Partner corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined Federal-Quebec general corporate rate (Federal 15% Part I + Quebec 11.5%); the Limited Partnership (CA_LP) is fiscally transparent under ITA s.96, so the headline rate applies only at the partner level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday available to the LP itself. Effective relief: (1) Federal small business deduction for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporate partners producing a combined Federal-Quebec rate of approximately 12.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; (2) Quebec refundable innovation tax credits (e.g., C3i, E-Business legacy credits) if the royalty-financing activities qualify as Quebec-based innovation; (3) enhanced treaty-based reductions on outbound payments to non-resident partners where a complete NR302/NR301 package is on file; (4) deferral through partnership fiscal period matching.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T5013-SUMMARY (Partnership Information Return) filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through CRA-approved electronic filing software (e-file/NETFILE tier) or a registered tax preparer; the partnership must hold a CRA business number program account ending in 'P'. Quebec does not require a separate provincial partnership return because the T5013 data is exchanged with Revenu Quebec under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end is due by May 31 of the following year). A Canadian partnership with non-resident partners or with gross revenue of CAD 2,000,000 or more, or assets of CAD 5,000,000 or more, is required to file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the Limited Partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact fiscal year-end; the allocation date used for each non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Limited Partnership exactly as registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Quebec registration certificate; a foreign-managed LP must use its registered Canadian legal name.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA business number (9-digit BN) with program account type 'P' for the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partnership carrying on business in Canada must obtain a BN and a Quebec establishment number before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Province or country where the principal business is carried on and the jurisdiction of the partnership's main permanent establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 'QC' for a Quebec-managed LP; a foreign partnership must identify its foreign jurisdiction and attach the Schedule identifying non-resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reason-for-filing code: 1 = new partnership; 2 = normal annual filing; 3 = short fiscal period; 4 = cessation of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use code 2 for the annual return; use code 3 for the initial stub period when the LP is formed mid-year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue of the partnership for the fiscal period, including all royalty/revenue-based financing receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Canadian-source revenue-based financing fees; non-resident partners' shares are separately allocated on Schedule 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets of the partnership at the end of the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box triggers the mandatory filing threshold for a 'Canadian partnership' with CAD 5,000,000 or more in assets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Per-partner allocation of income/(loss), capital gains, and 'at-risk' amounts, including each non-resident partner's share of Canadian business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source business income separately; such share is taxable under Part I on a net basis, not Part XIII withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file T5013: minimum penalty of CAD 100, plus CAD 25 per day per partner up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 under ITA s.162(7.1); a further penalty may be imposed for repeated non-compliance; Quebec interest accrues on any partner-level provincial tax triggered by the unreported information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T2 (T2 Corporation Income Tax Return) filed by a corporate partner of the LP with the CRA through e-file; the corporate partner carrying on business in Quebec also files Revenu Quebec Form CO-17 through clicSÉEQ. A non-resident corporate partner carrying on business via the LP must file a T2 to report its Canadian-source business income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the corporate partner's taxation year-end; quarterly instalments of estimated Part I tax are due on the last day of each quarter for the current-year tax obligation; instalment relief is available where the partnership has already remitted on behalf of the partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before taxes, including the corporate partner's share of the LP's business income computed under the rules of ITA s.96.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner must compute Canadian business income from the LP under the same rules and must complete Schedule 1 for its prorated share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting prior-year non-capital losses and other adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim a treaty allocation only to the extent the Canadian-source income is attributable to a permanent establishment in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part I tax payable, computed at the federal general rate (15%) or small business rate (9%) as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner may claim a foreign tax credit for the Canadian Part I tax against its home-jurisdiction tax; attach the relevant treaty residence certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of the unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; a repeated late-filing within 3 years raises the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month; additional Quebec late-filing penalties and daily interest under the Tax Administration Act (Quebec) apply to the provincial portion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NR4 (Non-Resident Tax Withholding Return) comprising NR4 supplementary slips and an NR4 Summary, filed with the CRA; Part XIII tax remittances are made electronically through CRA My Payment using the non-resident withholding program account ending in 'X'. The LP (as payer) must file NR4 slips for each non-resident partner to whom income is paid or credited.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Part XIII withholding must be remitted no later than the 15th day of the month following the month in which the amount was paid or credited to the non-resident partner; the NR4 Summary and slips are due on or before March 31 of the calendar year following the year of payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classification of each payment to the non-resident partner (e.g., partnership income, interest, royalty, dividend).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Characterization is decisive: revenue-based financing receipts may be treated as business income or as interest/royalty; the treaty article invoked depends on this code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of Part XIII tax withheld at the statutory 25% rate or the reduced treaty rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 25% unless a complete Form NR302/NR301 and the partner's Tax Residency Certificate are already in the payer's records; otherwise under-withholding creates personal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt payments (e.g., arm's-length interest meeting the exemption under ITA s.212(1)(b)(vii) or treaty-exempt royalties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only complete Box 22 where the statutory exemption or a reasoned treaty position is documented; a non-resident partner not carrying on business in Canada must not receive a Box 22 exemption for financing fees that are Canadian business income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold and remit Part XIII: the LP is liable for the entire unremitted amount plus interest; late remittance penalties escalate (approximately 3% for 1-3 days, 5% for 4-6 days, 7% for more than 7 days) and are followed by daily compounding interest; the CRA may also assess penalties for failure to file NR4 slips.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII (ITA s.212(2)) for dividends paid by a Canadian resident to a non-resident recipient; treaty-reduced rates apply (e.g., 5% under the Canada-US DTA for a US corporate shareholder owning at least 10% of voting shares; 15% otherwise). Distributions by the LP to non-resident partners that are not attributable to a Canadian business carried on in Canada are also subject to Part XIII at 25%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief is not automatic. Protocol: (1) the non-resident partner or recipient completes CRA Form NR302-R (corporations) or NR301 (individuals) and delivers it to the Canadian payer/LP before payment; (2) the partner obtains a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction revenue authority and the Canadian payer retains it in its books; (3) the payer withholds at the reduced treaty rate only when the declaration is on file; (4) if 25% was fully withheld, the non-resident files Form NR7-R (refund application) within two years of the end of the calendar year in which the tax was paid, or files a T2 return for a Part I refund; (5) for larger structures, the CRA may require a certificate of compliance and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation before granting a reduced rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory Part XIII rate; treaty-reduced rates commonly 10% (industrial royalties) and 0% for certain copyright and software royalties under the Canada-US DTA. Interest: 25% statutory, but interest paid to an arm's-length non-resident lender is generally exempt from Part XIII under ITA s.212(1)(b)(vii) where the payer is a corporation and the interest is fully deductible; non-arm's length interest remains subject to 25% unless a treaty reduction applies (commonly 10% under the Canada-US DTA). Quebec imposes no separate non-resident withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 in transactions with any single non-arm's-length non-resident, or CAD 5,000,000 in aggregate with all non-arm's-length non-residents: exceeding either threshold triggers (a) mandatory T106 information return filing and (b) contemporaneous Local File documentation under CRA policy; a Master File is required for MNE groups with worldwide gross revenue of CAD 1,000,000,000 or more. The same thresholds apply for Quebec provincial reassessments.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec do not maintain a standalone codified Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code. Economic substance is enforced through (1) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245 and Quebec Taxation Act s.1079.1), (2) the 'misuse or abuse' jurisprudence, (3) sham and agency doctrines in partnership law, and (4) the OECD Principal Purpose Test (PPT) in DTA applications. A Quebec LP engaged in revenue-based financing for digital brands must demonstrate substantive management and control in Quebec, real employees, localized books and records, and arm's length capitalization; otherwise it may be recharacterized as a conduit or shell and lose access to treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (willful circumvention of Canadian income tax)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting revenue-based financing receipts and royalty/financing fees from the T5013 or T2 returns, issuing fabricated invoices to non-resident partners, suppressing the LP's books, or funneling profits to a zero-tax foreign partner without any arm's length allocation or Canadian substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under ITA s.239(1): fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 2 years; civil gross-negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2) equal to 50% of the understated tax; unabated interest on all arrears; seizure and sale of property under ITA s.224; Quebec adds parallel penalties under the Tax Administration Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner who 'assented to or acquiesced in' the evasion are jointly and severally liable for unremitted Part I and Part XIII amounts under ITA s.227.1; courts may pierce the corporate veil, order civil restitution, impose travel bans and passport surrender, and imprison directors for up to 2 years for tax evasion or up to 5 years for fraud under Criminal Code s.380.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a non-arm's length royalty, guarantee fee, or interest rate to a non-resident parent or affiliated financing entity outside the arm's length range while the Canadian LP claims the deduction and the non-resident receives reduced-tax or exempt income, without contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under ITA s.247(2) adding the adjustment amount to the LP's income; penalty under ITA s.247(3) equal to 10% of the net upward adjustment where documentation is incomplete or the taxpayer fails the reasonable-efforts defense; interest under ITA s.161; T106 late-filing penalties and CAD 25,000 fines for record destruction; Quebec reassessment and penalties follow the same adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are assessable under ITA s.227.1 for any withholding that becomes unremitted after the deductions are disallowed; in aggravated cases criminal tax evasion charges, travel bans, and passport surrender follow; the LP's separate legal personality may be disregarded where it is found to be a sham or mere conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the revenue-based financing fund (NAICS 525990) without a FINTRAC Money Service Business or Restricted MSB registration where the activities constitute prescribed financial services, failing to conduct client due diligence/KYC on digital-brand borrowers and funding recipients, neglecting ongoing transaction monitoring of direct-debit ACH and wire transfers, and failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) or Terrorist Property Reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) of up to CAD 1,000,000 for individuals and CAD 2,500,000 for entities per violation (higher amounts may apply to large money services businesses based on gross revenue); criminal indictment carries imprisonment for up to 5 years; FINTRAC may suspend or refuse Quebec registration; Revenu Quebec and the AMF (Autorite des marches financiers) may impose separate provincial sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Every director, officer, or partner who 'directs, authorizes, assents to, acquiesces in, or participates in' the AML offense is personally guilty of an offense and liable to fines and imprisonment under the PCMLTFA; travel bans, asset-freezing orders, and civil restitution orders may issue under proceeds-of-crime legislation; the corporate veil is pierced when the LP functions as the alter ego of its controllers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham and GAAR Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Quebec LP with no offices, staff, or genuine management in Quebec while the general partner is a shell in a zero-tax jurisdiction, causing royalty/revenue-based financing income to escape Canadian taxation and stripping profits through inflated financing fees to tax havens, without real economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment under ITA s.245 and Quebec Taxation Act s.1079.1 denying the entire tax benefit; gross-negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2) equal to 50% of the tax understated where misrepresentation is established; the non-resident partner may be deemed to carry on business through a permanent establishment subject to Part I tax on a net basis; treaty benefits are denied under the Principal Purpose Test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are personally exposed under ITA s.227.1 for all unremitted Part XIII and Part I taxes; criminal fraud charges under Criminal Code s.380 may be laid for sham conduit arrangements; courts may order civil restitution, impose travel bans, require passport surrender, and pierce the corporate veil where the LP is an instrumentality of its founders.
